production.title: The Rise of Anthropic Explained Simply

narration:
This is Anthropic.
Soon it will go public at a $2 trillion valuation.
The biggest IPO ever on Earth.
Bigger than SpaceX and Saudi Aramco.
But how did it actually get this big?
Wasn't this just the company that made Claude?
How did it become the company leading the AI revolution?
Well, it all started with a kid named Dario.
Dario Amodei grows up with 2 parents who take their work seriously.
In their house, having a moral compass matters more than anything else.
He's also very good at science, like annoyingly good.
Then his father dies from hepatitis C.
And suddenly, the universe feels much less important.
Why couldn't science save him?
A few years after his father's death,
a new treatment pushes the disease cure rate from 50% to 95%.
A few years earlier, and his father would still be alive.
That thought never leaves him.
So, he begins looking for something that can search faster than any human.
Introducing artificial intelligence.
After working at Baidu and Google,
Dario joins OpenAI in 2016 and eventually leads its AI safety team.
The goal?
Build a machine that understands language, not one built from rules, one that learns.
So, they build something they call GPT, generative pre-trained transformer.
Feed it a mountain of books and articles and
make it guess the next word over and over, billions of times.
But, as OpenAI feeds it more data and gives it more computing power,
something strange happens.
Show people 2 AI answers.
Ask which one is better.
Repeat this thousands of times until it stops behaving like an idiot.
This is called reinforcement learning from human feedback or RLHF.
It works, but it treats the symptom, not the disease underneath.
Then, OpenAI builds GPT-3.
It is roughly 100 times larger than GPT-2.
It can write articles, answer questions, translate languages,
and perform tasks nobody specifically taught it to do.
So, after 4 years, Dario walks out.
His sister, Daniela, OpenAI's VP of safety and policy,
and several senior researchers walk out with him.
So, they make an impossible bet.
Prove the safest AI can also become the most powerful.
In 2021, Anthropic raises $124 million.
So, they begin building their AI, Claude, around a new idea.
Constitutional AI.
Instead of paying an army of humans to correct every bad answer forever,
you give the model a written list of principles, a constitution,
and train it to check its own homework against that list.
Early Claude is safe, mostly because it refuses to do anything remotely suspicious.
Then November 2022 arrives.
Cryptocurrency exchange FTX has collapsed.
Billions of dollars in customer funds may be missing.
OpenAI releases ChatGPT.
It reaches 1 million users in 5 days,
and becomes one of the fastest growing consumer products in history.
Anthropic releases Claude a few months later.
Claude is careful, helpful, easier to control.
Yet, the public responds, "Meh, just another ChatGPT."
Claude cannot win by becoming a second, slightly more polite ChatGPT.
It needs to do something ChatGPT flatly cannot do.
First, memory.
Most chatbots can only hold a limited amount of information at once.
Give them too much, and they begin forgetting the beginning before reaching the end.
So, Anthropic expands Claude's memory from around 9,000 tokens to 100,000.
In human language, that means Claude can process roughly 75,000 words at once,
about the length of an entire book, 3 times bigger than ChatGPT.
Then the giants arrive.
Amazon announces an investment of up to $4 billion.
Google commits billions more and gives Anthropic access to its custom AI chips.
Introducing Claude 3.
They do not release one model, they release us 3.
Haiku, fast and cheap.
Sonnet, smarter but still affordable.
Opus, the giant expensive brain you call when Sonnet starts sweating.
And Opus beats GPT-4 and Google's Gemini Ultra on
many of the major tests published at launch.
Then one engineer realizes something.
What if Claude stopped being a chatbot that helps people to work,
yet do the work itself?
September 2024.
Boris Chen joins Anthropic.
In February 2025, Anthropic releases the tool as a research preview.
It is called Claude Code.
Developers stop asking for little pieces of code.
They begin assigning complete jobs.
Claude is no longer just answering workers.
It is beginning to act like one.
In 2025, Anthropic receives a Pentagon contract worth up to 200 million dollars.
Anthropic allows most of it, but it keeps 2 restrictions.
No mass surveillance of Americans and no weapons that
can choose and kill targets entirely by themselves.
The Pentagon cancels Anthropic's agreement.
Anthropic's prospectus, dated November 10, 2026,
says Claude revenue grew from 0 at its commercial launch in the first
quarter of 2023 to $17.0 billion for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026.
Then a number begins spreading around Wall Street.
$2 trillion.
Investors immediately divide into 2 groups.
$2 trillion?
Anthropic may need to spend hundreds of billions on chips just to keep up.
You're pricing Anthropic as if Claude has already won.
No.
I am pricing what happens if it does.
Anthropic has shown that a company built around AI
safety can reach the front of the race.
Going public does not complete that bet.
It makes the bet much harder.
Every delay angers investors, and every refusal appears in the stock price.
Whether Anthropic's principles can survive Wall Street remains to be seen.
Follow the channel.
As a wise man once said,
"A principle isn't a principle until it costs you money."

research.summary: Anthropic’s rise is best explained as a reinforcing business system, not just a chatbot launch. The company combines frontier-model research with enterprise software, cloud distribution and large infrastructure commitments. Better models attract more business usage; usage produces revenue and operational feedback; revenue and financing fund more chips, data, engineering and safety evaluation. The evidence supports explaining this flywheel, but it does not prove Anthropic will remain the market leader.

claims.claim: Anthropic’s prospectus, dated November 10, 2026, says the company was founded in 2021 and that Claude revenue grew from zero at its commercial launch in the first quarter of 2023 to $17.0 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026.
claims.source_title: Anthropic Prospectus

claims.claim: Anthropic says its revenue comes from customers using Claude through its platform and applications, with pay-for-intelligence, subscription and combined pricing. A growing number of enterprise customers sign annual or multi-year contracts with minimum-spend commitments.
claims.source_title: Anthropic Prospectus — Revenue Model

claims.claim: As of September 30, 2026, Anthropic reported more than 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in trailing-twelve-month revenue, up from more than 950 one year earlier. Those customers generated 74% of trailing-twelve-month revenue, according to the prospectus.
claims.source_title: Anthropic Prospectus — Customer Growth

claims.claim: Claude is available through Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure. Anthropic says these partnerships let enterprises deploy Claude inside infrastructure, security boundaries and purchasing arrangements they already use, while the cloud providers’ sales teams extend Anthropic’s distribution.
claims.source_title: Anthropic Prospectus — Cloud Partnerships

claims.claim: Anthropic announced a $65 billion Series H funding round at a $965 billion post-money valuation on May 28, 2026. The company said the money would support safety and interpretability research, additional compute and expanded products and partnerships.
claims.source_title: Anthropic Raises $65B Series H at $965B Valuation

claims.claim: The prospectus shows why frontier AI requires substantial capital: compute and infrastructure expenses reached $9.9 billion in the three months ended September 30, 2026, equal to 58% of revenue. Anthropic also reported $5.0 billion of compute under short-term commitments and a $567 million operating loss for that quarter.
claims.source_title: Anthropic Prospectus — Compute Costs and Operating Results

claims.claim: Anthropic and Amazon announced an agreement for up to five gigawatts of additional capacity for training and deploying Claude. Anthropic said it would commit more than $100 billion to AWS technologies over ten years, while Amazon announced a $5 billion investment with up to $20 billion more possible in the future.
claims.source_title: Anthropic and Amazon Expand Compute Collaboration

claims.claim: Anthropic said in 2026 that it trains and runs Claude across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs and NVIDIA GPUs. It described this hardware diversity as a way to match workloads to suitable chips and improve performance and resilience, while its Google-Broadcom agreement adds multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity expected to come online starting in 2027.
claims.source_title: Anthropic Expands Google and Broadcom Compute Deal

claims.claim: Research on language-model scaling finds that model performance depends systematically on model size, training-data size and training compute. Follow-up work found that, under a fixed compute budget, model size and the number of training tokens should be scaled together, illustrating why frontier progress requires balancing chips, data and model capacity rather than buying only larger models.
claims.source_title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models; Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models

claims.claim: Anthropic’s model-development process includes capability, safety and alignment evaluations. Its published evaluation guidance emphasizes testing different risk categories, reporting uncertainty and running evaluations continuously during development rather than treating them as a one-time check before release.
claims.source_title: Building Strong Safety Evaluations

core_fact.fact: Anthropic’s official prospectus, dated November 10, 2026, says Anthropic was founded in 2021 and that Claude revenue reached $17.0 billion for the three months ended September 30, 2026.

metadata.title: The Rise of Anthropic Explained Like You're 5
metadata.description:
This is the story of Anthropic, Claude, and Dario Amodei—and how a safety-first AI startup became one of the biggest companies in the AI race.

Free guide to this video (steps and every source): https://studio.golidee.com/guides/golide-long-2026-11-28.pdf

From leaving OpenAI and building Claude to raising billions from Amazon and Google, Anthropic made an impossible bet: that the safest AI could also become the most powerful. This video explains how that bet turned into a fight with ChatGPT, a booming Claude business, Claude Code, and a massive IPO.

But can Anthropic’s AI safety principles survive Wall Street?

Chapters
0:00 Intro
0:39 From Physics
1:47 The Safety Bet
3:13 Finding An Opening
4:22 The Public Bet
5:47 Close
